question.text: A physical quantity <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi></math> is represented by the formula <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo>=</mo><msup><mi>m</mi><mn>2</mn></msup><msup><mi>r</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>4</mn></mrow></msup><msup><mrow><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi mathvariant="italic">g</mi></mrow><mi mathvariant="italic">x</mi></msup><msup><mi>l</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mfrac><mn>3</mn><mn>2</mn></mfrac></mrow></msup></math> If the percentage errors found in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>y</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">,</mo><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi>m</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">,</mo><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi>r</mi><mo mathvariant="italic">,</mo><mo mathvariant="italic"> </mo><mi>l</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>g</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>18</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>0</mn><mo>.</mo><mn>5</mn><mo>,</mo><mo> </mo><mn>4</mn></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math> respectively, then find the value of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>x</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>p</mi></math>.
